## 0.32.0 — real hands (2026-10-24)

The hero, Mira and the Hollow have real hands: grown out of the arms, with fingers that bend. Update both the game and
the server to v0.32.0.

### New
- **Hands with fingers.** Every finger has three joints and the thumb its own, and the hand is one skin with the arm
  (no more rigid fist stuck on the wrist). Each hand grips what it holds: the fingers close round the haft of an axe or
  pick, a club, mace or torch, a spear shaft, a blade's hilt or the bow's riser, each at its own thickness.
- An empty hand hangs open and relaxed; it closes into a fist for a punch or an unarmed guard, and round the rungs on
  a ladder.

### Changed
- **The iron helmet** is rebuilt: a taller rounded spangenhelm rising to a slight point, the brow band on the forehead
  above the eyes, ridges along the dome, and the nasal lying on the bridge of the nose (it was a squat dome with the
  nose guard floating in front of the face).
- **The hips** are the widest part of the body again and run smoothly into the thighs (the thighs bulged out of them,
  with a notch at each side), and the seat is a little fuller.
- **A bed needs a room.** You sleep in it only once it stands in a sheltered room: a roof over it and walls round it
  (a doorway or a window is fine, an open side is not). Out in the open it says so. You can still claim it anywhere,
  to wake there.
- **The tanning rack may stand on a plank floor**, so you can build a roofed workshop round it and keep it curing in
  the rain (it had to stand on bare earth).

### Fixed
- **No more creatures in the water.** Stalkers, spiders and the rest came up in pools, the tarn and the shallows and
  walked about on the bottom. They now only appear on dry ground, wander back out of the water, and a roaming pack
  waits on the shore while its round crosses water.

## 0.31.0 — in good stride (2026-10-24)

The hero and the people of the frontier move like people: new walking, running, sprinting and sneaking, arms that hang
naturally, and tool swings that stay on their own side. Update both the game and the server to v0.31.0.

### Changed
- **Walking, running and sprinting are new.** Each foot is set down and stays put while the body passes over it,
  rolling from the heel onto the ball of the foot, and the steps match your speed at every pace, so the feet no longer
  skate. The hips sway and turn, the shoulders turn against them and the head stays level; a sprint leans in further.
- **Sneaking** is a steadier crouch: hips back, the back bent and the head up, the arms hanging forward and loose, with
  soft rolling steps.
- **Arms and shoulders.** At rest the arms hang off the body with soft elbows and the hands beside the thighs (the hero,
  Mira and the Hollow). They used to hang stiffly against the ribs with the forearms jutting straight forward. Weapon
  and fist guards keep the elbows out and the forearms angled in.
- **Chopping and mining.** The axe goes up beside the head and over the right shoulder and comes down in front of the
  right side; the pick hangs behind the shoulder before it drives down to the rock. The other hand balances on its own
  side. Before, the arms crossed in front of the chest on the way down.
- **A lit torch is carried raised** beside your head; other tools hang from the hand at rest.
- **New hands.** A real fist: four fingers with knuckles wrapped round the handle, and a thumb over them, for the hero,
  Mira and the Hollow (it was a flat block with stubs under it). The wrist stays straight in the swing; it used to bend
  sharply down at the blow.
- Mira and the Hollow walk the same way; the Hollow drags its left foot.

### Fixed
- **Every animation plays at its proper pace.** The moves of the hero, Mira and every creature were imported a quarter
  too slow, so a blow showed a moment after it landed and the end of many moves was cut off. They now match the game.

## 0.30.0 — light below (2026-10-22)

Light to carry into the Underhearth, and ground down there that is no longer bare. Update both the game and the server
to v0.30.0.

### New
- **Light to wear.** Three pieces glow in the dark and light the ground round you with one soft light high over your
  head: enough to see the ground by, never enough to dazzle. They only show in the dark (below, in a crypt, at night),
  and **sneaking shades them**, because a lit hero is a seen hero.
- **Glowcap Circlet** (head, workbench: 2 leather, 4 glowcaps, 1 obsidian): a leather band with glowcap stones on the
  brow, a cold blue light.
- **Emberlit Lamellar** (chest, forge level 2: 6 iron bars, 4 ember ore, 3 leather): iron plates gone ash-dark with
  seams of ember that never cool, and a rune plate on the breast. Armour 18, a little more than iron lamellar.
- **Wisp Rune** (charm, workbench: 2 Echo crystals, 3 glowcaps, 2 ember ore): Kaunan, the torch rune, cut in an Echo
  crystal. It floats over your shoulder, sheds sparks and gives the brightest light of the three. Skills grow 5% faster.
- **The Underhearth's ground grows.** Under the glowcaps a carpet of **glow-threads** whose bulbs pulse blue and violet
  and sway with the air; **ash reeds** with ember-lit tips out on the ash; sparse **cinder reeds** in the Cinder Wastes and
  blood-tipped reeds on the Dominion's shore; basalt pebbles and little **sprigs of glowing crystal** everywhere (fire
  crystal on the glass field). Nothing grows in the lava.

### Changed
- **The air below**: glowcap spores drift blue and violet in the woods, and embers rise over the Wastes and the
  Dominion's lake. The Vale's dust and falling leaves no longer drift down there.

## 0.29.0 — the fallen dominion (2026-10-22)

The Underhearth's third land, east of the Cinder Wastes: the Fallen Dominion, the city of the people who lived down
here before the Keepers came. Update both the game and the server to v0.29.0.

### New
- **The Fallen Dominion**: a basin round a lake of fire, and on an island in it the Black City, black towers with fire in
  their windows round a stepped temple. A tier 5 land ("Infernal").
- **The Ash Road** runs to it from the east side of the Cinder Wastes, through a canyon lit by old lamps and under the
  ruined Ash Gate.
- **The Broken Causeway.** The west causeway to the city breaks off over the fire. A Keeper pedestal at the break takes
  three Echo crystals and raises an Echo of the span, for everyone in the world. The long way round is the south
  causeway, through **the Fallen Gate**, the Dominion's fortress.
- **The Dominion's dead**: *Sentinels* in black plate (slow, very hard to stagger; a mace dents the plate where blades
  skid), some of them standing as **statues on the old posts until you come too close**, and *Acolytes* who keep their
  distance and throw fire that sets you alight (frail up close).
- **Four lore tablets** tell what the Dominion was, what the Keepers took from it, and what burns in the sky down here.
- **The Last Forge** in the Black City tempers a weapon or tool already worked to +3 to **+4** (2 ashsteel, 3 ember ore
  and a fire opal): finally a use for ember ore beyond the wards.
- **Finds**: ashsteel (from Sentinels), Dominion relics (Orm pays 22 silver each), Sentinel and Acolyte trophies, three
  Keeper coffers in the city and the fortress, and a fifth ward stone, the Ward of the Ash Road.

### Changed
- The Underhearth's map shows the part of it you are in (the Wilds and the Wastes, or the Dominion), each with its own
  fog of war. What you uncovered in v0.28 stays uncovered.
- Orm now buys fire opals (12 silver each).

## 0.28.0 — the world beneath (2026-10-22)

The first part of a second world under the Vale: the Underhearth, and its first two lands, the Ashen Wilds and the
Cinder Wastes behind them. More lands will follow behind their cliffs. Update both the game and the server to v0.28.0.

### New
- **The Throat and the fracture.** In a hollow under the Stoneteeth's north crests stands a ring of Keeper stone round a
  bottomless well, with a dead lift hanging in it. Beside it the rock is split open, and old steps go down.
- **The way down is walked.** The fracture leads into a tunnel, then a gorge cut into a cliff, out onto the Overlook high
  above a land with its own horizon, and down a ramp of black rock to the floor.
- **The Underhearth's sky.** No sun and no night down here: a roof of star-crystals and a red glow low in the south-east
  that never sets. The sky has states instead of times of day: *Emberglow* (the usual), *Ashfall* (ash falls like
  snow and the distance closes in), *Bloodstorm* (red lightning and wind; elites far more often, and ember seams yield
  more) and the *Hollow Silence* (the glow drains away and hunting packs find you sooner).
- **The Ashen Wilds**: woods of giant glowcaps and twisted gloomtrees with turquoise or red leaves, grey ash fields,
  black basalt, two slow rivers of lava with crusted bridges, a pool of fire in the middle, the bones of something
  huge, black spires, and a keep hanging upside down from the sky with four chains running down from it to the Landing.
  A sealed Keeper door stands in the north wall.
- **The Strider**, a creature taller than the Courtyard's walls, walks the far north of the Wilds. It ignores you, the
  ground shakes where it steps, and Ashhounds near its feet lose interest in their prey.
- **Creatures**: *Ashhounds* (pack hunters of the ash; fireproof, weak to cutting blows), *the Kindled* (burning dead
  whose blows set you alight and who burst into flame when they fall) and *Ashhorns* (great grazers that leave you
  alone unless you hurt one). The Wilds are a tier 4 land ("Merciless"), and their hunting packs track you here too.
- **Heat.** Lava burns hard and throws you back out. The air beside it scorches, and in a Bloodstorm it is hot out in
  the open. The glowcap woods are cool. A hot hero breathes slower and does not heal on their own. Burning (a Kindled's blow, the lava) goes out sooner if you roll.
- **The Keepers' lift.** At the Landing, wake the lift's platform with a touch. From then on it carries you up through
  the hanging keep to the Throat and back down.
- **Resources**: obsidian and ember-ore seams (iron pick), basalt boulders, emberwood from emberbark and gloomtrees (iron
  axe), glowcaps, brimstone crust, ash pelts.
- **Recipes**: Glowcap Broth (hearth: a meal that keeps the heat a step further off), Frostlichen Draught (herbalist's
  table: six minutes without the heat), Obsidian Arrows (workbench: the sharpest arrows), Brimstone Fire Arrows.
- **Keeper wards**, the havens below: inside a lit ward nothing hunts you, wounds close as at home, and you can build
  (walls, a roof, a bed to wake in, chests, a campfire). The Landing's ward is lit; two ward stones in the Wilds wait to
  be rekindled with 3 ember ore and an Echo crystal.
- **The Sealed Door** answers once both wards of the Ashen Wilds burn: put a hand to it and it sinks into the floor.
  Behind it a canyon runs north through the wall.
- **The Cinder Wastes**, the Underhearth's second land: a plain of ash and slag under a redder sky, cracked with narrow
  fissures of lava, strewn with skeletons. It is a tier 5 land ("Infernal": creatures ×2.15 health and ×1.85 damage; the
  HUD wants 30 armour), and the whole plain is hot. In a Bloodstorm it scorches unless you shelter under a roof or in a
  ward. Far off on its northern rim stands a ruined fortress, still out of reach.
- **Vents.** The Breathing Flats and the plain round them are full of vents that rumble, glow, then roar a column of fire
  that throws you up and sets you alight. A ring on the ground warns you; roll through or wait.
- **The Fallen Titan**, a skull and spine larger than the Strider, lies in the west of the Wastes; the Kindled keep it.
  Three Keeper coffers lie with dead wardens out on the Wastes, and a third ward stone, the Cinder Ward, waits to be
  rekindled.
- **New creatures**: *Slagbacks* (Chargers grown over with slag: they charge faster and leave the ground burning
  behind them; blades and arrows turn on the slag, a mace breaks it) and *Cinder Crawlers* (spiders of cinder and
  glass that run straight in, leap, and set you alight; they hunt in swarms and an arrow finds their gaps).
- **Fire opals**, from the opal seams beside the vents (iron pick), Slagbacks and Cinder Matriarchs. New charms at the
  workbench: the *Fire Opal Charm* (the heat a step lower, burning goes out twice as fast) and the *Slag Charm* (from an
  elite Slagback's trophy: +35% stagger, +6% damage).
- The map shows the Underhearth's own map while you are down there, with its own fog of war.
- Down below the wind gives way to a low drone, and the lava bubbles.

### Changed
- The Stoneteeth's north crests have a level hollow where the Throat stands. In an existing world, a site that stood
  there moves out of the hollow (it keeps what it holds and whether you solved it), and nothing grows inside it.
- Fire Arrows can also be made with brimstone instead of resin and flint.

## 0.27.0 — hard country (2026-10-21)

The outer lands are dangerous now, not just a little tougher, and the fixes from a code review of combat, building and
co-op. Update both the game and the server to v0.27.0.

### Changed
- **Every land has a danger tier**, shown as skulls by the place name: the homestead is safe (0), the forest 1, the
  Frontier, Birchwood and the coast 2, Elderwood and the Mire 3, the Stoneteeth Highlands and the Skerries 4
  ("Merciless"). When your worn armour is thin for the land, the HUD says so beside the skulls (below 8 armour in a tier
  2 land, 17 in tier 3, 27 in tier 4). Each outer land says how hard it is the first time you walk in.
- **Creatures of the deeper lands are much stronger.** Born in Birchwood or on the coast: ×1.35 health and ×1.25
  damage (it was ×1.3 / ×1.2 in every outer land). Elderwood and the Mire: ×1.65 / ×1.45. The Highlands and the
  Skerries: ×1.9 / ×1.65. They see further (up to 30% in tier 4), move a little faster and come as elites far more often
  (up to 2.5 times as often as in the Vale).
- **Packs between the old haunts.** Birchwood, Elderwood, the Mire and the Highlands had big stretches with nothing in
  them; new packs stand about every 50-60 m deep inside each, with the land's own creatures (Stalkers and Chargers; the
  dead in Elderwood by day too; spiders in the Mire). About half of the Stalker packs roam a loop of 35-55 m instead
  of keeping to one place. In Elderwood, the Mire and the Highlands every pack keeps one more at night.
- **Hunting packs.** Linger in Elderwood, the Mire or the Highlands (or in Birchwood at night) and something picks up
  your scent: a pack of the land's creatures comes for you from 40-55 m away, out of sight, and you are told where from.
  It happens about every three to five minutes out there, sooner at night; a roof or a fire overhead makes the scent go
  cold. Easy hunts less often, Hard more often, Builder never.
- **Creatures follow further and search.** A hunting creature keeps looking and listening for you. Out of its senses it
  goes to where it last knew you, then gives up ("?"), searches the spot and wanders home: after 5 seconds in the Vale,
  up to 11 in the Highlands. Break its sight and go quietly (sneak, or at least walk) to shake it off. It used to follow
  you anywhere within its leash, and gave up the moment you were 45 m from its den; the deeper lands now follow 35-80%
  further. A creature that notices you calls others of its kind from further away there (up to 19 m; 9 m in the Vale).
- **Wounds hardly close on their own in the wilds.** Without food, health comes back at 1.2 a second in the forest (as
  before), 0.6 in tier 2 lands, 0.3 in Elderwood and the Mire and 0.2 in the Highlands and the Skerries, and only after
  10 seconds unhurt out there. Eat before you go.
- **Freezing kills.** It used to stop at 15 health. The high crests of the Stoneteeth freeze by day too, not only at
  night. On Easy freezing still stops at 15.
- **A roll needs its full price** (16 stamina, less with Wolf's Stride; it started on 8), and a perfect roll gives back
  60% of it (it gave back 20, more than it cost).
- **A parry costs a little stamina and wears the weapon** (less than blocking the same blow). Out of breath, or with a
  broken weapon, a guard raised in time only blocks.
- **Second Wind is each hero's own** and the HUD shows whether it is ready or spent until dawn.

### Fixed
- **A roll or a Dash Strike no longer lasts while a menu is open.** Opening the satchel or the map mid-roll left you
  untouchable for as long as the menu stayed open.
- **Walls, doors and floors stop blows**, yours and the creatures': they struck straight through them. Ground slams
  (a Charger's stomp, a Hollow's slam, the Guardian's slam) still carry through. A spider's web is stopped by walls and
  trees, can no longer pass a hero between two frames, and no longer sticks after a successful roll or parry.
- **Felled trees stay gone in the distance.** Walking away from a felled tree brought its silhouette back on the
  horizon.
- **Building: no more free materials or practice.** A piece that saved you a material (the Building skill) gives back
  one less when taken down, and putting a piece back where one was just taken down teaches nothing.
- **Co-op:**
  - two players taking the same piece down at once both got its refund; the second now gives it back;
  - the bloomery and the tanning rack carry on for whoever joins or reconnects later (they got the station as it was at
    the last load or take), and garden beds keep their growth and rain watering;
  - Mira's batches are kept by the server: they survive the player who handed them over leaving, only that player's
    game does the work, and anyone else who takes over gets the rest back once;
  - when the player who woke a barrow crypt leaves, its dead and its Warden stay for those still below (the Warden used
    to vanish, so the grave goods could not be unsealed).
- A cell of the world queued for loading is skipped when nobody is near it any more (after a teleport or a fast boat).

## 0.26.0 — sure footing (2026-10-21)

Movement and fighting with more weight, after a closer look at how Valheim moves its players, and Dash Strike paid for
in breath. Update both the game and the server to v0.26.0.

### Changed
- **A calmer pace.** The jog is 4.8 m/s (was 5.2) and the sprint 7 m/s (was 8.2); Running practice adds up to 12% to the
  sprint. A sprint drains 10 stamina a second (was 11). Stalkers and spiders still catch a jogging hero, and a sprinting
  one still gets away.
- **Movement has momentum.** You speed up and slow down over a fraction of a second instead of at once, and a run turns
  in a curve: the faster you go, the wider the turn. Turning right round at a sprint plants your feet and brakes first.
  The body turns more slowly at speed too.
- **A little more air.** A jump rises about 1.45 m (was 1.25) and hangs a moment longer. Out of breath you still hop,
  just lower, instead of not jumping at all. Falls hurt from the same height as before (4 m free).
- **Dash Strike costs 20 stamina** (less with practice in the weapon in hand; it was free) and is refused when you are
  out of breath. It carries about 4.5 m (it went 7.5 m and slid on for 3 more).
- **Shadow Step** (blades) costs 22 stamina, less with practice, and needs all of it to start (it started on 12 and took
  25).
- **Heavy blows and weapon arts need their whole stamina cost** to start; light swings still start on less.
- **Blows land more fairly:**
  - a swing goes for the creature most in front of you (where you push the stick, or where the camera looks when you
    stand still), not just the nearest one off to the side;
  - it keeps turning after that creature through the wind-up and the blow, so a quick one cannot step out of the way
    as easily;
  - it strikes through the whole of the swing, not in one instant: a creature that steps in a moment late is still hit;
  - it reaches a creature's body, not only its middle, so the flank of a big beast (a Charger, the Guardian) counts.
- The view widens less while sprinting (4 degrees, was 7) and trails you a little more.

### Fixed
- **Build mode: the piece you aim at no longer disappears.** Aiming a piece at a wall (a roof at a wall that already had
  one, for example) made the wall vanish until you looked away: its support tint used a shader variant the game did not
  include. The support colour is now a thin see-through layer over the piece, and it reads more clearly too.

## 0.25.0 — the Skerries (2026-10-21)

Islands out in the sea and a boat to reach them, chests worth opening, crates on the tideline, and every land with its
own air. Update both the game and the server to v0.25.0.

### New
- **The Skerries.** Four islands lie out in the corners of the sea, past wading depth, with bare sea stacks between them:
  - **Gullholm** (north-east): a tall rock white with gulls. Their nests on the ledges give eggs; a cairn and a sea
    chest wait on the summit.
  - **Wrecker's Holm** (south-east): a longship broken on the rocks, her sea chests still aboard. The drowned walk its
    beach at night.
  - **Selkie Strand** (south-west): dunes and tide pools. Seals haul out on the sand (and slip into the sea when you
    come close), mussels crowd the pools, amber lies in the dunes.
  - **Keeper's Light** (north-west): the Keepers' lighthouse. Climb the stair round the tower and kindle the old fire
    (10 wood, 5 resin): every island and sea stack appears on the map, the light burns over the sea at night, and the
    Keepers' coffer at the door opens.
- **The coracle** (workbench: 8 wood, 4 leather, 3 resin, 2 flax): a round hide boat you carry on your back. Wade out
  past your depth with one in your bag and you climb in. Paddle with the movement keys (sprint paddles hard, for
  stamina) and run into any shore to step out; the boat goes on your back again. It turns back from rocks and from the
  swell at the edge of the world; storms slow it and push it along. In co-op the others see you paddle.
- **The sea wind.** Afloat, or out on the Skerries, nights, rain and storms chill you, and a storm freezes you when you
  are soaked or afloat. A fur mantle, a warming draught or the Selkie's Pearl keeps it off; bone broth helps.
- **Chests by land, Valheim style.** A chest rolls a few finds, each picked by weight from its land's table, never the
  same thing twice: Birchwood chests hold cloudberries, flax and barley; the Mire's spider silk, bog iron and bones; the
  Highlands' frost lichen and iron; the Elderwood's amber and oak; the Skerries' silver, mussels and pearls. Better
  chests hold more, and sometimes silver.
- **Four kinds of chest:** the traveller's chest, a sailor's **sea chest** (four or five finds, often a piece of gear),
  the Keepers' **coffer** (always a good piece of gear) and the **washed-up crate**.
- **Flotsam.** Every three days the sea washes seven crates up on the beaches of the Vale and the Skerries, each tide in
  other places. Whoever opens one first opens it for everyone.
- New finds: **Gull Eggs** (Gullholm's nests), **Mussels** (the tide pools; now and then one holds a pearl) and the
  **Pearl** (Orm pays 14 silver).
- New meals: **Steamed Mussels** (hearth: 4 mussels, 1 moonpetal; two bowls, a light meal that heals well, 8 min) and
  **Egg Bannock** (hearth: 2 gull eggs, 3 barley; two, much more stamina for 11 min).
- New charm: **Selkie's Pearl** (workbench: 2 pearls, 3 silver, 1 leather): the sea wind cannot chill you, a coracle runs
  a quarter faster, breath comes 5% quicker.
- **Each land has its own air**, after Valheim's environments: a blue-teal mist under the Elderwood's canopy, the Mire's
  green haze, cold clear light on the Highlands, warm gold over the Birchwood, bright sea air on the coast and the
  Skerries. The fog's colour and thickness, the ambient light, the sun shafts and the colour grade ease from one land's
  air to the next as you cross.
- **The sea moves:** long swells roll in from the south-west, lines of surf run up the beaches, white caps show when the
  wind is up.
- **Fires cast shadows** at the Ultra shadow setting: the nearest fire within 18 m casts soft shadows.
- The place line names the island you stand on, and the map names the islands once you have found them.

### Changed
- Wading out to sea until it turns you back now says how to reach the islands.
- Performance: creatures wandering near you (not hunting) take about half the work they did.
- Story progress in co-op travels as only what is new. Every discovery used to send the whole chronicle and every lore
  text to the server, and the server sent it all back to everyone, which grew with every evening played.

### Fixed
- **One server, one profile, whatever you call it.** Joining the same server as `localhost` and as `127.0.0.1` (or by
  its name and by its IP address) made two copies of your hero there, and an old satchel could come back through the
  other one. Each server world now has its own id and your profile for it is kept by that. The profile you already have
  moves over the first time you join. A world started anew on a server (a new world file) gets a new profile.

## 0.24.0 — hush and hearth (2026-10-20)

Creatures that look and listen, blows that matter by kind, homes worth furnishing, three meals at once, and woods that
grow in glades. This release also brings everything from **0.23.0 — steady fires** below (rejoining, recent servers, a
sturdier server), which was not released on its own. Update both the game and the server to v0.24.0.

### New
- **Sneaking.** Left Ctrl (L3 on a controller) crouches. Sneaking is slow and quiet: creatures see you from about half as
  far (less by night or underground, unless a torch burns in your hand) and hardly hear you. An eye under the compass
  shows whether anything is hunting you. Sprinting, jumping, climbing or sitting stands you up.
- **Creatures look and listen.** They see what is in front of them, not through rock, trees or walls, and hear all
  round: sprinting carries furthest, walking much less, and chopping, mining and fighting a long way. One that notices
  you shows a **!** and calls the others of its kind close by. Once it has been in a fight it looks all round.
- **Sneak attacks.** A creature that has not noticed anyone takes three times the blow (arrows too). The same creature
  can only be taken unawares once every few minutes.
- **Damage types.** Clubs and fists crush, blades and axes cut, spears, picks and arrows pierce. Stalkers are weak to
  cuts; Chargers to piercing (and they resist crushing); Hollows to crushing (they resist piercing); Mire Spiders to
  crushing (they resist cuts); Greyhorns to piercing; the Guardian to crushing (it resists piercing). Weak spots take
  half as much again, resisted blows about a third less; the numbers show it in colour.
- **Creatures in the journal:** every kind you have fought, with what it is weak to and what it shrugs off.
- **Comfort.** Furniture near where you rest makes Rested last longer: 8 minutes, plus one minute for each comfort
  level. You start at 1; a roof over you adds 1, and so does the best piece of each kind within 10 m (a seat, a bed, a
  table, a rug, a banner, a light, a trophy, a painted shield, a fire; the weapon rack, rune stone, Keeper column and
  dragon cross each count on their own; the chandelier counts 2). In the open only a fire counts. The build menu shows what
  each piece adds, and the Rested line shows your comfort.
- **Sneak skill:** practised sneaking near creatures that have not noticed you, and by sneak attacks. It makes you
  harder to see and lets you sneak faster.
- **Light and shadow matter when sneaking.** Open sunlight gives you away; the shade of a rock, a wall or a roof, the
  night and the dark underground hide you. Fires, lanterns and torches light you up, your own torch too.
- **Awareness marks while sneaking:** over each creature near you, a pale eye if it has not noticed you (gold when your
  next blow would be a sneak attack) or a red **!** if it is hunting you.
- **Three meals at once.** Eat up to three different meals: each adds stamina and healing. A meal's stamina fades as it
  wears off; you can eat it again, or let a new dish take its place, once it is half gone. The status line lists each
  meal with its time left, and a meal's details show its stamina, healing and how long it lasts.
- **Build mode shows support on built pieces:** the piece you aim at takes on its support colour, blue-green when well
  carried, through yellow to red near failing.
- **Feet stand on the ground** on slopes and steps (your hero and other players): the hips drop for the lower foot and
  the knees bend for the higher one.
- Video settings: **Distance blur** (far hills soften out of focus; nothing within 60 m) and **Colour fringe** (a faint
  chromatic edge towards the corners). Both on by default.

### Changed
- **Meals** give about 60% of their old stamina and healing each, since three can now be eaten together (three good
  meals reach about 180 stamina).
- **Falls** go by height: up to 4 m is free, then the damage rises to 100 at 20 m. A 9 m drop costs about 31 (it was
  about 64), and drops of 3-4 m no longer hurt.
- **Breath comes back faster the emptier the bar:** twice as fast from empty as near full. A refill from empty takes as
  long as before.
- Nothing can be built where a hero stands.
- **Rested** heroes learn every skill a quarter faster.
- A bench indoors rests you with a fire basket burning near, not only by a hearth or campfire.
- Greyhorns let a sneaking hunter come about half as close as a walking one.
- **L3 on a controller crouches** instead of toggling the sprint; hold B to sprint.
- The woods grow in glades and thickets: the Birchwood, the Elderwood and the Mire are denser in places and open in
  others (the Vale's forest already was).
- No trees stand on cliffs and scree, and nothing to forage grows on ground too steep to stand on.
- Some things now grow together: rings of redcaps in the old woods, patches of cloudberries in the Birchwood, stands
  of flax in the open, lichen crusts in the Highlands.

## 0.23.0 — steady fires (2026-10-19)

Co-op that holds together: clearer joining, a way back after a dropped connection, and a sturdier server.
Update both the game and the server to v0.23.0.

### New
- **Rejoin.** When the connection to a server is lost, choose **Rejoin** to go straight back in. A server that is
  restarting or updating is tried again for about a minute; Back stops trying.
- **Recent servers** on the join screen: the last four you joined, with their players, latency, whether they need a
  password and whether their version matches yours. Pick one to fill in its address and password; Forget removes it.
- **Connection line** over the party list: your latency, and a warning when the server has gone quiet.
- **V** is a heavy attack too, for keyboards without a middle mouse button.

### Changed
- Joining shows what it is doing (connecting, receiving the world, building it). Big worlds no longer time out while
  they are still arriving.
- A version mismatch says which side is behind. When your game is older, an **Update** button sits on the join screen.
- Being removed from a server says so; a server shutting down tells you it is restarting instead of "connection lost".
- Joins, leaves and server announcements also go into the chat log.
- The updater shows how many MB have arrived, can be cancelled, and gives up on a download that stalls.
- The pause screen's server card lists players one per line and shows a live latency.
- The changelog, the Controls screen and Settings > Controls scroll with a controller's right stick (and the d-pad
  where nothing is selectable).

### Fixed
- **Felled trees, broken rocks and picked plants stay that way for everyone**, including players who join later and
  after the server restarts, until they grow back. They used to stand again for anyone who had not seen them fall.
- A hero made in the seat of a forgotten hero no longer takes over that hero's server profile (name, gear and all).
  Forgetting a hero (or a Hardcore fall) now also forgets their server profiles on this machine.
- A player whose connection dropped can join again at once; they were refused as "already in the world" for 30 seconds.
- A dead connection is noticed within 25 seconds instead of leaving the world frozen.
- A server world that cannot be loaded returns you to the title with a message instead of an endless loading screen.
- Creatures could stand frozen and unhittable after their area changed hands at the moment they appeared.
- After a server reset, a returning hero no longer appears at their spot in the old world (in the sea or a cliff).
- Other players' names show as plain text (formatting codes in a name drew on everyone's screen).

### Server
- One invalid position or time from a client could stop every later save until a restart; such values are ignored.
- A damaged world file is put aside and the newest readable backup is loaded; if none can be read, the server stops
  with a clear message.
- Connections that have not said hello are limited, kept small and closed after 15 seconds; a client that stops
  reading is dropped at once. Chat and commands are limited to a few lines a second and logged on one line.
- Bans also record the player's public address (not a local, private or tunnel one, which many players can share).
  The game clock and autosaves follow a steady clock (a system clock change
  could stop the time of day or delay autosaves). `-timeout` sets the drop time (10-300 seconds).

## 0.22.0 — waters and harvests (2026-10-19)

Includes the draw-and-shelter improvements first staged in the v0.21.0/v0.21.1 drafts: deliberate bow drawing and
arrow arcs, isolated local/server saves, deletable map/death-loot markers, roof/gable joins, recoverable arrows,
persistent hotbar hover, dragging items back to the satchel and the visible money-pouch balance.

### Changed
- Heavy attacks use the middle mouse button. Hold right mouse (or C) to block; right mouse also cancels a bow draw.
- Left Shift only sprints. Dodge with Left Alt or mouse button 4; controller controls are unchanged.
- Thin the added shoreline flint deposits, with a stronger reduction around home and Mira's campsite.
- Developer god mode keeps health and stamina full, including while attacking, sprinting and drawing a bow.
- Developer fly mode walks normally on the ground and follows descending slopes. Jump to take off; landing ends
  flight until the next jump. Flight speed boosts apply only while actually flying.
- Crops take game days to ripen after watering: barley 2 days, flax 2.5, redcaps 2.75 and moonpetals 3 before bonuses.
  Growth prompts show game days. Existing plantings keep their growth percentage when loaded.

### Fixed
- Mire water blends smoothly with the surrounding biome and offshore sea instead of changing at rectangular edges.
- Dedicated flint deposits appear on dry banks beside the tarn, brook, bog pools and ocean coast, on the visible ground.
- Character-preview decorations no longer intercept equipment-slot hover, and its rotation area avoids the slots.

## 0.21.1 — draw and shelter follow-up (beta, 2026-10-18)

### Changed
- **Left attack draws the bow; right attack cancels.** Releasing left attack looses the arrow. Running out of stamina
  cancels without firing or spending an arrow. Release the draw button before drawing again after a cancellation.
- The **Money pouch** button shows its current silver balance and updates after transfers and spending.

### Fixed
- Intact world arrows have a recovery prompt and a proper 2.4 m automatic pickup radius. A full satchel can still
  recover one into an existing partial arrow stack. Broken shafts disappear quickly instead of looking collectible;
  the existing 60% survival chance for non-fire arrows is unchanged.
- Hotbar hover stays highlighted in the inventory, including across its periodic refresh.
- Drag gear or consumables from the hotbar back into the satchel. Returning the held weapon removes its binding and
  equipment together; if the bag is full, the whole change is refused safely.

## 0.21.0 — draw and shelter (beta, 2026-10-18)

### Changed
- **Bows reward a deliberate draw.** Drawing takes longer and slows movement. The aiming circle shrinks as the string
  comes back; early shots scatter widely. Better bows, quality, upgrades and archery skill improve handling. Holding at
  full draw costs more stamina, rising the longer you wait, and eventually makes your aim shake.
- Arrows follow a stronger arc over distance. Base damage is unchanged; a fully drawn shot has a **95% critical chance**
  on a successful hit, dealing 50% more damage.
- **Local and server adventures are separate.** Local worlds live in `Saves/Local`; each server has its own hero profile
  under `Saves/Servers`. Gear, satchel size, supplies and progress stay with that adventure. An existing server hero is
  restored on the first visit after upgrading; a new server starts with a one-time copy of the selected local hero.
  Older local saves and their backups are copied into the new folder, with the originals kept for recovery.

### Fixed
- Quitting online can no longer write the server's buildings and world over a local save after disconnecting.
- The controller's map cursor is hidden in mouse mode, removing the apparent pin that survived deletion.
- Click an existing custom pin to edit it; right-click to remove it. Right-click a fallen satchel marker to hide its
  map and compass marker without removing the loot. Controllers can hide satchel markers from the map list.
- Roof Slopes and Ridge Roofs turn and join at their actual low/high edges, including a raised ridge between two slopes.
- Ridge Gables can stack on Gable Walls; their occupancy and structural support are tracked separately.

## 0.20.0 — a place for everything (2026-10-18)

### New
- **Map pins and waypoints.** Click the map to place a pin, or move its cursor with a controller's right stick and
  press X. Select a pin to label it, remove it or toggle its waypoint. Up to two waypoints can be active on the
  compass; home is always marked. Pins are saved with your hero, including when playing online.
- **Money pouch.** Put loose silver in the pouch from the inventory. It uses no satchel space and the trader can
  spend it directly. Withdraw one, a stack or all that fits to store silver in the shared stash or give it to someone.
- **Shared stash filters:** All, Equipment, Materials, Consumables and Valuables. Use the Filter button, or LT / RT.
- **Chargers stomp** when you crowd or circle their flanks: a marked circle warns of the blow and its knockback.

### Changed
- **Satchel space now matches the cells.** Spare gear takes one slot. Worn gear appears only in equipment, and bound
  gear only on the hotbar; neither uses a satchel slot. One stack of up to 20 per bound consumable sits on the hotbar;
  further stacks remain in the satchel. Full bags cannot take off gear or clear a hotbar slot without making room.
  Mouse hover and controller focus compare spare gear with what is worn.
- **Chest:** 10 wood, no flint. **Woodpile:** 100 wood, recovered when taken down.
- **Flint is found near water:** the tarn, brook, bog pools and coast, rather than scattered across dry land.
- **Torches are fragile:** 25 base durability (was 140). Their damage and burning are unchanged.
- The same meal cannot be eaten again while Fed until its last 30 seconds. A different food can replace it.
- The Keepers' seal also requires every recruitable companion to have joined the homestead (currently Mira).
- A crypt's burial-hall gate stays shut after the first enemies fall. Open it yourself when ready to face the Warden.

### Fixed
- The build-piece menu scrolls within the screen; the selected piece's description and cost remain visible.
- Satchel and stash grids show the actual free slots, without extra empty cells from rounding the last row.
- Transfers preserve the storage panes' scroll positions, even when sorting moves the transferred item elsewhere.
- Sleeping through the night always grants Rested, in single player and co-op.
- Other heroes' claimed beds cannot be used for sleeping or claimed over.
- Water reaches the noisy shoreline near Grove of Svartmark instead of ending in a straight, dry strip.

## 0.19.0 — the island and the seal (2026-10-18)

### New
- **The Vale is an island.** The ring of mountains round the edge is gone: the land runs down to a coast (sandy
  beaches in the west and south, a marshy shore where the Mire meets the water, cliffs under the Stoneteeth) and the sea
  goes on to the horizon. You can wade out until the water reaches your chest; the cold sea turns you back there. You
  hear the surf long before you see it.
- **The Keepers' seal.** The Courtyard gate no longer opens for anyone: the Keepers sealed it, and the seal asks for
  proof before it lets you at the Guardian. Walk all four outer lands, slay a barrow's Warden in its crypt, light a
  watchtower's five fire baskets, wake the Gale relic and forge the Ember relic; then forge a **Keepers' Key** at the
  forge from amber, frost lichen, spider silk and cloudberries (and iron and crystal) and set it in the seal. Examine
  the seal at the gate's rune stone to see what is done and what is not. Once broken, the gate stays open. (A world
  whose Guardian already fell is open as before.)
- **Ladders.** A narrow **Ladder** leans on a wall or the edge of an upper floor, its foot on the ground or floor
  below; stack them for more storeys. A **Step Ladder** stands on its own with a little platform on top, one storey
  up: climb it to reach a roof. Walk into a ladder to get on (or press E), W / S to climb, Space to let go; at the top
  you step off onto the deck or the platform. Walking towards a ladder from the deck above takes you down it.
- **Build mode works like Valheim's.** B opens build mode on the piece menu with the mouse pointer; click a piece and
  the menu folds away to the piece in hand while you aim. B or Tab brings the menu back, Esc leaves build mode. The
  mouse wheel and 1-5 still step through the pieces. (A controller keeps the whole grid on show, as before.)
- **Snapping: pieces snap to the piece you aim at, and turn with it.** A roof aimed at an upper floor goes on that
  storey's walls (it used to drop onto the ground-floor walls, so the top of a two-storey house could not be roofed). A
  roof aimed at a wall goes over the room the wall closes, not out over the yard; once that is roofed, the next is an eave.
- **Roof slopes turn themselves**: the eave onto the wall, rising towards the ridge or along with the slope beside them.
  Gables turn to rise with the slope next to them. Rotating turns them on from there.
- **Walls carry on**: a wall aimed near the end of a wall goes on beside it; aimed at its top, it goes on top.
- **Furniture and stations set down by a wall** turn their back to it and stand right against it (they used to need a gap).
- **Hold Shift** (L3 on a controller) to place freely, without snapping; beams and posts then move on a finer 25 cm grid.
  The bar under the piece says SNAPPED or FREE.

### Changed
- **Balance:** tools fight at about half the damage of a weapon of their tier (the iron axe out-damaged the wooden
  club): Flint Axe 7, Iron Axe 11, Hallvard's Axe 15, Stone / Tusk / Antler / Iron Pickaxe 6 / 7 / 8 / 9. Chopping and
  mining are unchanged. The Iron Spear (19 → 17) and the Flint Spear (12 → 11) give up a little for their reach; the
  Iron Blades (8.5 → 9.5) and the Iron Mace (23 → 24) gain a little.
- **The tanning rack may stand under a roof**, and it needs to in bad weather: wet hides do not cure while it rains on
  the rack. A lean-to over it keeps it working.
- Mira's voice stops when you leave a conversation with Esc (only Goodbye stopped it), and not when you pick an answer
  that she starts to speak.

### Fixed
- **Mira's first choices in the forest** (asking what happened, offering salve or linen) froze the game for a few
  seconds and did nothing.

## 0.18.0 — voices of the Vale (2026-10-16)

### New
- **Mira speaks.** Everything she says out loud (her greetings, advice, the lore of the Vale, her whole story, the
  wounded stranger in the forest) is voiced. Settings > Audio > Spoken dialogue turns it off.
- **A whole new set of sounds**: every creature has its own voice (the Stalkers' snarls and yelps, the Chargers' squeals,
  the Guardian's footfalls and roar, the barrow dead rasping below ground, a Warden's roar), and so do doors, chests,
  building and taking down, landing, eating and drinking, planting and harvesting, foraging, the tanning rack, lore
  stones, solved puzzles, the crypt gate, new lands, omens and your hero's grunts and breath. Footsteps are recorded
  boots on grass, dirt, wood, stone, mud and snow. Fires crackle, a smelting bloomery roars, the forge and the cooking
  pot sound while you work at them, elites hum, and ravens call over the woods.
- **Ridge Roof and Ridge Gable**: a steep ^ roof over a single square, with the pointed gable that closes its ends. The
  whole roof of a one-room hut in one piece.
- **A pointer in build mode**: press **Tab** to bring the mouse pointer over the piece panel. Hover a piece to read it,
  click it to pick it (and go back to aiming), click a tab to switch. Tab, Esc or the right button puts it away.
- **The game has its own mouse pointer**, a bronze arrowhead, instead of the Windows arrow.

### Changed
- **Hallvard's Hearthstone faces the fire**: its carving used to face away from the camp.
- **Online, the Esc menu has no Save** (your hero is saved as you play and when you leave; the server keeps the world).
- Releases, the update check and the AMP template now all live in one place,
  [jeatheak/forgotten_frontier_amp](https://github.com/jeatheak/forgotten_frontier_amp). Server hosts on AMP: see the
  wiki's new Hosting pages (AMP and the dedicated server).

### Fixed
- **The chat line no longer covers the chat**: the line you type sits under the log, at a size that fits it.

## 0.17.1 — wayfarers, mended (2026-10-16)

### Changed
- **The guard covers the front** (70° to either side), not the flanks: being surrounded matters again.
- The game starts faster (its sounds are made a few at a time), and build mode, the HUD, the inventory and the name
  plates do less work each frame.

### Fixed
- **Joining a server no longer strips your hero.** Worn gear and the hotbar came through a join as loose gear in the
  satchel (since 0.15). They are worn and on the hotbar again, as they were when you left.
- **A felled tree stays felled** (and a broken rock broken, a picked plant picked) when you walk away and come back: the
  land used to grow everything back the moment it was out of sight. Things grow back in their own time, and a saved game
  remembers them.
- **Sitting on a bench or stool that is taken down** no longer leaves the hero frozen in the seat.
- **A crash while saving can no longer lose a hero.** Every save keeps the previous one as a backup, and a save cut short
  is read from it.
- **Co-op:** the Guardian no longer vanishes for good when everyone has left the courtyard and someone comes back; two
  players taking the same piece of gear from the chests, the same bars from a bloomery or the same load of a station no
  longer get it twice (the second hand is told someone was quicker and gets back what it paid); taking more from a chest
  than was left (two hands at once) is evened out in the satchel too; falling and jumping heroes move smoothly; a
  server's clock can only be changed by its moderators.
- **Fair fights:** the Hollow's second chop is marked on the ground like the first; the Guardian's and the Charger's
  charge marks are as long as the charges; elites and the big Bog Weaver are as large to hit as they look; creatures no
  longer appear inside walls or water, or right under a hero; the dead now rise around a hero standing at the barrow, as
  they were meant to; a creature far from everyone falls to the ground instead of hanging in the air.
- **A hit just before a long fall** no longer cancels the fall damage. The fire paths cannot be interrupted by a blow.
- **The hero's thoughts are your own:** in a shared world one player's thoughts no longer silence everyone else's, and a
  newcomer to an old world still gets theirs.
- A Mira batch saved before 0.17 resumes as the right recipe; silver from a sale is saved when you close the trade;
  Second Wind refreshes with the day the clock shows; footsteps on boulders, cliffs and ruins sound like stone; a
  controller's sticks ease in past the dead zone; Alt+Tab no longer rolls the hero; Back gives up on a join that hangs;
  loot still lying about is kept when you save and quit.
- **Server:** one malformed connection can no longer stop the server unsaved; a bad port or bind address is reported
  clearly; the server saves once on shutdown, after everyone's last position is in.

## 0.17.0 — wayfarers (2026-10-16)

### New
- **Block and parry with your weapon.** Hold **MMB or C** (LT on a pad) with a club, spear or blades to guard: a blow from
  the front is mostly stopped (a club 70%, a spear 60%, blades 50%) for stamina, and an empty stamina bar breaks the guard.
  Raise the weapon **just as the blow lands** to parry it: nothing gets through and the attacker reels, open to a strike.
  Fists, tools and the bow cannot block. Mira's old lesson is now the **Riposte**: a parry strikes back at once.
- **A trader.** Orm the Peddler keeps a cart by the Birchwood road, west of the old ruins. He buys wood, stone, hides,
  ore, trophies and what the outer lands give for **silver**, and sells a **bigger satchel** (and draughts, arrows,
  whetstones, bandages and seed barley). His camp is a safe place: creatures do not hunt there.
- **Each outer land has its own find:** cloudberries in Birchwood, spider silk in the Mire (nests and the spiders
  themselves), frost lichen on the Highland rocks and amber in the roots and heartwood of the Elderwood oaks. New with
  them: the Cloudberry Tart (a meal for quick breath), the Silk Bandage (60 health at once), Lichen Tea (two Warming
  Draughts) and the Amber Charm (skills 10% faster, breath 10%). The Horn Bow is strung with spider silk now.
- **The hero's thoughts.** Now and then your hero thinks out loud, one quiet line, about what might come next: a tool, a
  bed before nightfall, the trader, a land not walked yet, at last the Guardian. Each thought comes once and never in a
  fight. Settings > Gameplay > Hero's thoughts turns them off.
- **Server moderators.** A server's Moderators setting (hero names or client ids) marks players as moderators: they show
  as **[MOD]** and can type **/kick**, **/ban**, **/unban** and **/say** in the chat. Everyone can type /players and /help.
  A welcome message, bans that are kept, and Kick / Ban / Make Moderator in AMP's player list.

### Changed
- **The satchel has room for 15 things** now, up to 20 of a kind in a slot (gear is strapped on and needs no slot). What
  does not fit is set down at your feet; loot on the ground waits until you have room. The trader sells more room, up to
  40 slots.
- **Chests hold 10 slots each** (20 of a kind in a slot, a piece of gear a slot). All chests still open the one household
  store, so every chest you build adds 10 slots.
- **The build menu** is a solid panel on the right with the whole tab at once (no more paging through rows), names in
  bold white that read over any ground, and the piece's description, cost and what you have in a clear block under it.
- **Longer evenings.** The sun sets at 20:00 instead of 18:00 and full dark comes about two hours later; the night is
  shorter to match.
- **The outer lands are harder:** creatures there have more health, hit harder, notice you sooner, come more often as
  elites, and the packs are bigger. The Vale itself is unchanged.
- **Creatures move smoothly:** they speed up and slow down instead of switching direction in a single frame, Stalkers and
  spiders circle without flipping back and forth, and in co-op the creatures another player's game runs glide instead of
  jumping.
- **Dash Strike is learned, not known from the start:** it comes once any fighting skill (unarmed, clubs, spears, blades or
  archery) reaches 10.
- **Woodcutting:** the axe is raised over the right shoulder before the chop (the arms used to cross).
- **Footsteps** sound like boots on what is underfoot (grass, earth, wood, stone, snow, mud, water); spiders tick and
  click instead of sounding like boots.
- **Fine weapons shimmer in your hand** (a glint runs along good, fine and masterwork weapons in their quality colour); the
  shimmer in the satchel is gone, and armour does not shimmer. Buffs show faintly on the hero: honed, rested, each tonic,
  the Gale and Ember relics.
- **The fire paths** flare: the signal fire reaches for you, a column of flame takes you and gives you back at the far fire.
- **The crafting book shows what arrows do** with your bow (at full draw and for a quick shot).
- **More to see in the lands:** fallen trunks and old stumps in the woods, cloudberry patches in Birchwood, mushroom rings in
  Elderwood, lichen boulders and cairns in the Highlands, gold and rust-red leaves on the wind, green wisps over the Mire
  and ice glittering in the Highland air.
- Co-op traffic is lighter: creatures standing still are sent once a second, and players far apart get each other's
  movement less often.

### Fixed
- **A roof could not be finished:** a roof piece over an eave or the middle of a wide house took its height from the ground
  under it instead of the roof beside it; it now lines up, and aiming at the side of a roof extends it sideways too.
- **Vigdis's camp (and any site at the foot of the rim mountains)** sat half inside the mountain: such sites move in
  towards the Vale until the ground round them is clear. (In an existing world those sites, and now and then one near them, stand somewhere new.)

## 0.16.0 — torchlight (2026-10-15)

### New
- **Torches.** Bind resin-soaked linen round a stick (2 wood, 1 pine resin, by hand) and carry it in your hand: it lights
  the dark around you for about nine minutes, and a blow with it sets creatures alight. A burned-out torch can be rekindled
  at a workbench (repair) or simply made again. Nights are also a little less black than before.
- **Health bars over creatures.** A small bar shows over every creature in a fight (with its level when it is above 1) and
  stays a few seconds after you hit it; bosses and elites keep the big bar at the top. Settings > Gameplay > Creature health
  bars turns them off.
- **Co-op chat, properly.** Chat has its own corner over the bottom left: the last lines stay a while and fade, all of them
  show while you type, and what a hero says also shows over their head. **On a controller, hold D-Up for quick chat**: pick
  a line ("Over here!", "Help!", "Follow me." ...) and it is said. A tap of D-Up still drinks a draught.
- **Drag things onto the hotbar.** In the satchel, drag a tool, weapon or consumable onto a hotbar slot with the mouse
  (right-click a slot to empty it). X (or 1-5) still works, and now also for **food, draughts, tonics, salves, whetstones
  and arrows**: a consumable on the hotbar is eaten, drunk or used when you press its key, and shows how many you carry.

### Changed
- **Felling trees pays.** Trees come down quicker, logs split quicker, and a felled tree gives about twice the wood: a
  birch about 8, a pine about 12, an oak about 6 oak wood (picking up a branch still gives 1 or 2).
- **The satchel** shows six things a row and says plainly that it has no limit (it never had one: it scrolls).
- **Building and the chests:** building has always taken what it needs from the chests as well as your bag; the build bar
  now says so and shows how much of each material you have in all.
- **The bow:** a click looses a quick, weak shot as soon as the arrow is nocked (a short click used to be dropped, so the
  left button seemed not to shoot), and the left button looses while you hold the draw with the right.
- **Creatures find their way round rocks.** They keep to the side they chose while they edge round something in the way,
  and one that is stuck takes a short detour instead of pressing on.
- **Release builds have no developer tools** (no Developer page, no F3), and neither does a shared world.

### Fixed
- **Felling a tree hurt you about every other time** when you stood close to the trunk: the falling tree now only crushes
  what is under it, from a stride beyond the stump.
- **The rank came again at level 20.** A skill's rank (Apprentice, Journeyman ...) is announced once, when you reach it;
  the other tens just name the level.
- **Waking inside a wall.** After sleeping (and after falling) you get up beside your bed where there is room to stand:
  the foot of the bed, else either side, else the head end.
- **The day did not count up after a night's sleep** if you went to bed after midnight. The day now begins at dawn, the
  way you count it: whenever you lie down, you wake on the next day.

## 0.15.1 — shared fires (2026-10-14)

### New
- **Make a hero for a server.** Without a hero, **Join a world** offers **+ New hero**: choose the name and look and you
  are back at the join screen, ready to go, instead of first waking in a Vale of your own. Played alone later, that hero
  sets out into a new Vale with everything they brought back.

### Changed
- The address and password boxes on the join screen now show clearly which one you are typing in (and its heading lights
  up).
- Co-op traffic is lighter: messages waiting together go out in one packet, and the server answers as soon as a message
  arrives instead of on its next tick.
- Servers: the difficulty setting now rules existing worlds too (from the next start), saves no longer hold the world up
  while they are written, and backups are kept every 30 minutes (a setting) instead of on every autosave, so they reach
  back hours instead of minutes.

## 0.15.0 — shared fires (2026-10-14)

### New
- **Co-op: play together in a shared world.** A small dedicated server keeps the world; up to four friends join it with
  **Join a world** on the title screen (address and password). Bring any of your heroes: they keep their bag, gear,
  skills and perks, take home what they find, and the server remembers where they stood for the next visit.
- **What you share:** everything built (beds, gardens and their crops, stations, doors), the household stash in every
  chest, things put down and the satchels of the fallen, the bloomery and tanning rack, the time of day, the weather of
  each land, and the story: the Guardian, the Beacon, puzzles, places found, the map and the chronicle.
- **Trees fall and rocks break for everyone**, and a picked plant is gone for all. The wood, stone or loot goes to whoever
  did the work.
- **Creatures are shared.** Each one is run by the nearest player's game; everyone sees the same creature, the same
  attack warnings and the same damage numbers. Your rolls and counters are always decided on your own screen.
- **Name plates** over the other heroes (with their health when hurt, "down" when downed), the party in the top left
  corner with how far away everyone is, and **chat** (Enter to talk). Downed friends can be helped up; music from a lute
  rests everyone who hears it.
- **Sleeping in co-op:** lie down and wait; the night passes once everyone is in bed (move to get up again).
- **Update in place.** When a new version is out, the title screen offers "update now": it downloads, checks and installs
  the new version and restarts the game. Your heroes and worlds are kept.

### Changed
- In a shared world nothing pauses (the menu says MENU, not PAUSED), perfect dodges do not slow time, the difficulty is
  the server's (Hardcore plays as Hard: one life is a single-player rule), and new sagas begin in a hero's own Vale.
- **Garden beds show their water:** the earth is pale and dusty while a planting waits for a drink, and turns dark and
  glistening once it is watered.

### Fixed
- **Bogwalker's Balm** and the **Warming Draught** had no picture in the bag.

## 0.14.0 — sagas and songs (2026-10-14)

### New
- **Difficulty**, chosen when you make a hero: **Builder** (always noon, always clear, nothing hunts you), **Easy** (the
  old rules: what you carried waits in a satchel), **Normal** (gear included in the satchel, creatures a little tougher),
  **Hard** (all you carry is lost but your weapon and chest armour, and your skills slip back a little) and
  **Hardcore** (one life). You can make it harder later from the pause menu, never easier. Heroes from earlier versions
  play on Easy.
- **A new saga.** Once the Beacon burns you can keep exploring, or begin again in a fresh Vale: at the same difficulty
  with a perk, or one step harder with a greater perk. Perks add up from saga to saga (more health, a second wind,
  quicker crafting, faster feet ...). The Beacon offers the choice whenever you visit it.
- **The lute.** Make one at a workbench with a shaving horse. Take it in hand and a small note panel opens: play real
  notes (three octaves), record a phrase and it loops, then layer more over it. Play standing and you sway with the
  tune; play sitting on a bench or a log and you stay seated. Music by the fire leaves everyone who hears it rested.
- **The outer lands bite.** Mire spiders' bites carry **venom** and the webs hold you fast; a **Bogwalker's Balm**
  keeps both off. Out on the **Highlands** it is **cold** (and freezing at night, in a storm or soaked): wear a fur
  mantle, drink a **Warming Draught**, or keep to a fire. A cap or a bowl of bone broth helps.
- **Station extensions bring new work:** the shaving horse opens the horn bow, the antler pickaxe and the lute; the
  grindstone fire arrows and cheap whetstones; the smith's rack the iron mace and the lamellar; the quench trough the echo
  attunement.
- **The frontier remembers its war:** charred palisades, spears in the turf, burnt carts, bones in the grass, and here and
  there a heap of timber still smouldering.
- **Charms are worn:** amulets hang on a cord round your neck, totems are tied to your belt.
- **Finer gear glows** softly in its quality colour in your bag and on the hotbar, and fine and masterwork weapons shed
  the odd mote of light.
- **Sort the bag and the stash** (Z / L3): by kind, A-Z, amount or quality.
- **Camera zoom:** the mouse wheel (Ctrl + wheel while building), or hold the right stick in and push it up or down.
- **A loading screen** with painted art, the game's own logo on the title and as the app icon, and no Unity splash.
- **Developer tools:** "Noon and clear" holds the sun at midday and keeps the sky clear.

### Changed
- **Balance:** upgrades give +10% each (was +15%), fine and masterwork a little less, weapon skill +40% at 100 (was +50%);
  the iron blades and their whirlwind hit less hard; the Guardian has more health and hits harder; creatures are tougher
  on Normal and Hard.
- **Finer gear costs more to improve:** good ×1.25, fine ×1.5, masterwork ×2 the materials.
- **The forest is denser**, with thickets and more rock; the Highlands carry far more snow, and up there the rain falls
  as snow.
- **Benches** have their backrest at the back and seat two. **Wells** are open, with water deep inside, and the roof sits
  on its posts.
- **Snapping beams:** rotating turns the piece through all four directions, and it snaps to the point under your cursor.
- **Esc leaves build mode** (a second Esc opens the pause menu).
- **Mira walks round** stations, chests and walls (and through doors) instead of through them.
- **The map marker** for you has a dark disc and a pulsing ring, so it stands out on top of home.

### Fixed
- **Horn Bow** could not be sent to Mira, and showed "At station" with materials for several.
- **The grindstone's wheel** swung round in the air in a big circle.
- **The palisade gate** hung centred on its post and swung about its middle; it now hangs in the frame and swings on the
  left post.
- **Build ghosts** showed blue fire sculptures (the echo brazier's flames): ghosts are the structure only now.
- **The camera** slipped out through windows while building inside.
- **The pond below Stranger's Camp** had water over only half of it (at the edge of the Mire).
- **A volatile elite's death blast** showed its red ground circle even with attack warnings off.
- **A blow landing as you fell** (a whirlwind at 0 health) still dealt damage.

## 0.13.0 — first guests (2026-10-13)

### New
- **Stillwater Tarn**, a clear pond about a hundred paces west of the homestead, fed by a brook from the hills. A trodden
  path leads there from the fire. Wade in to fill a bucket.
- **Water looks like water.** Ripples, the sky and the sun reflected in it, depth you can see into, foam along the shore
  and a running current on the brook. The bog's water is dark and peaty, with drifting duckweed.
- **The map shows water** in blue, so you can find somewhere to fill a bucket.
- **The Mire is dangerous now.** **Mire Spiders** and **Bog Weavers** nest among the webs: they keep their distance, spit
  webs that slow you, then dart in to bite. The bog is full of fallen trunks, webs that catch you as you walk into them,
  egg sacs and glowing mushrooms. A low mist drifts over the water, bubbles rise out of the peat, and at night pale
  lights hang just out of reach. The bog dead walk in the fog by day too, and the Mire counts among the worst lands.
- **Talk to Mira** at the homestead: ask her for advice, what she can do for you, about the Vale, where to find water,
  and hear **her story** a chapter at a time as you see more of the world.
- **Send Mira to a station.** At the homestead, pick a recipe in the crafting book and choose **Send Mira**: she walks
  to the herbalist's table, the workbench or the fire and makes it, and it goes into the stash. (Not from out in the
  wild.)
- **Beds are claimed.** Each hero claims one bed (claiming another frees the old one) and wakes there.
- **Mira needs a bed of her own.** Once her wound is treated she joins only when there is a free bed under a roof at the
  homestead.
- **Exploration music** for the meadows, the forest, Elderwood, the Highlands and the Mire, with quiet stretches
  between tracks.
- **What's new** on the title screen (this list), shown once after each update.

### Changed
- **Controller build mode works like the inventory:** LB / RB switch tabs, d-pad left/right picks a piece (hold it to keep
  moving), d-pad up/down changes row. **Hold D-Down** to open or close build mode; LT rotates, RT places, Y takes down.
- **Display settings wait for Apply.** Pick a display mode and resolution, press Apply, then keep it (it switches back by
  itself after 12 seconds if you don't).
- **Fullscreen is borderless** by default. Exclusive fullscreen is still there, marked as such.
- **Healing draughts have a 30 second cooldown** (it was one second).
- **Comparing gear:** equipping or crafting shows each stat against what you wear now, green when better, red when worse.
- **Crafting shows how many you can make** with what you carry and have in the stash.
- **Upgrades** no longer show the ×1 / ×5 / ×10 / ALL amounts (an upgrade is always one).

### Fixed
- **Freeze after alt-tab in fullscreen.** In exclusive fullscreen the game could keep piling up frames while it was in the
  background until the whole PC ran out of memory. It now draws almost nothing while in the background.
- **Dark grass patches** that followed the camera when you stood below grass on a slope.
- **Dead creatures** no longer stand in the way of the fight.
- **Inside a crypt** you no longer see prompts for trees on the surface (the "Chop" oak), creatures on the barrow above no
  longer hunt you from up there, and you no longer hear them.
- **The crypt entrance** is an open, dark doorway again (the mound's turf filled it).
- **Camps on slopes:** the bones, crates and tents no longer float above the ground.
- **New music files** play (they were in the wrong folder and format).

## 0.12.0 — bone and bowstring (2026-10-13)

### New
- **The Barrow Hollow:** the barrow dead rise at night. They raise a shield against blows from the front, chop twice and
  leap at heroes who keep their distance, and their blades carry **grave rot** (no healing until a wound salve draws it
  out). The crypt Warden is now a huge Hollow lord.
- **The Greyhorn:** herds of great grey elk that bolt together; a wounded bull turns and charges.
- **Archery:** hold to draw, release to loose. Hunting Bow and Horn Bow, Flint, Bone, Iron and Fire arrows.
- **The Stonecutter** and a stone building kit: walls, arches, floors, stairs, pillars and low walls.
- Palisade and gate, trophy mounts, hide rug, stool and weapon rack.
- 16 new items and 22 recipes: bone, grave iron, antler, venison, new meals, a grave ward tonic, charms, a whetstone and
  bone meal for the garden.
- New skills: **Archery** and **Building**.

### Changed
- Faster grass, animation and creature AI (better frame rate in busy areas).

## 0.11.0 — many hands (2026-10-13)

### New
- **Music** for the title, hero creation and the homestead by day and by night.
- **Batch crafting** (×1, ×5, ×10, ALL); Mira can finish work at the herb table, workbench and fire when you walk away.
- **Watering:** buckets, rain on open beds and a well. **Wet** from rain and wading.
- More building: quarter floors and walls, gable walls, flat roofs, beams, posts, hanging lanterns, a chandelier, fire
  baskets, rune stones, a well; painted cloth banners.

### Changed
- Only the pause menu pauses the game. Alt-tab keeps it running.
- Stations show their progress and time left while they work.

## 0.10.0 — raise your own roof (2026-10-12)

### New
- Build the old hall yourself: storeys, stairs and **structural integrity** (pieces far from the ground need support).

### Changed
- The clearing starts empty (no longhouse). Split-screen removed (online co-op is planned instead).
- Combat balance and many smaller fixes.

### Fixed
- A crash in the text engine.

## 0.9.0 — hearth and hall (2026-10-11)

### New
- **Barrow crypts:** a stair under each barrow leads down to halls, a gate and the Warden.
- Stations and chests are build pieces now; roofs, doors that swing open, full refunds when taking pieces down.
- Fall damage from high drops.

## 0.8.0 — the deep frontier (2026-10-11)

### New
- **Skills** that grow as you use them, **gear upgrades** +1 to +3, **station extensions**, **farming** in garden beds.
- **Elite creatures** with traits, **day omens**, **site puzzles** (singing cairns, watch braziers), the fire paths, and
  **Hallvard's trail**.

## 0.7.0 — by the fire (2026-10-11)

### New
- **Sit by the fire** to rest and become Rested.

### Changed
- Stamina matters again; easier-to-follow menu focus on a gamepad.

## 0.6.0 — hearth and hall (2026-10-11)

### New
- Jumping, rolling and sprinting; calmer, weightier combat; hunting and cooking; the Gale shrine puzzle; developer tools
  (F3).

### Fixed
- Tools fell trees and break rock again.

## 0.5.0 — sharper edges

### New
- Stadia controller support and rumble; new beards, hair and hands; chunkier pixel textures; clearer attack effects.

## 0.4.0 — the wider world

### New
- A world four times larger with four outer lands (Birchwood, the Mire, the Stoneteeth Highlands, Elderwood), generated
  per hero; points of interest, weather and a map that fills in as you explore.

## 0.3.0 — survival update

### New
- Start with nothing: gather, craft tools and gear with stats and quality, build stations and a bed, save to one of three
  heroes at the title campfire.
